metadata.title: क्या हुआ जब मैने दुनिया का सबसे कड़वा खाना खाया | I Tasted the Most Bitter Food in the World
metadata.description: Oma Bador Narzi is one of the most celebrated dishes of the Bodo community, recently honoured with a Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2024. This unique delicacy is prepared by slow-cooking pork with dried jute leaves, giving it a distinct bitter flavour that sets it apart from other meat dishes. Far from being just a taste acquired by tradition, the bitterness of Uma Bador Narzi carries health value — it is known to help regulate blood sugar levels and is particularly beneficial for managing diabetes. Deeply rooted in the culinary heritage of the Bodo people, this dish is more than food; it is a testament to how tradition, health, and culture blend on a single plate.
